title: French Bistro à Deux Board
seo_title: French Charcuterie Board for Two: Pâté, Brie & Baguette
description: A French bistro charcuterie board for two: Brie de Meaux style brie, Comté, pâté de campagne, saucisson sec, baguette, salted butter, cornichons and Dijon.
hook: Paris without the plane ticket: a bistro plate of pâté, cheese, bread and butter for two.

items.name: Brie de Meaux style or Camembert
Jambon de Paris or saucisson sec

why: A French charcuterie plate is simple on purpose: a soft cheese, a firm one, pâté and a dry sausage, with bread and butter. Creamy brie and nutty Comté cover both cheese styles, and country pâté with saucisson sec covers both meat styles.
Cornichons and Dijon are the sharp, sour notes that cut the fat, and radishes with salted butter are a very French snack on their own. Green grapes or a pear and a Beaujolais keep it light.

timeline.what: Take out the pâté and ham; soften the butter.
Slice the baguette at the table.

faq.q: What's on a French charcuterie board?
faq.a: Brie or Camembert, Comté, pâté de campagne, saucisson sec or jambon de Paris, baguette, salted butter, cornichons, Dijon mustard, radishes, grapes or a pear and walnuts.

faq.q: What wine goes with a French board?
faq.a: Beaujolais (Gamay) or a Côtes du Rhône. Both are fruity and light enough for pâté and soft cheese.
The CDC advises against refrigerated pâté during pregnancy. Shelf-stable canned pâté is the safer choice, or skip it.
